precepts.text: He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow. Delivering the fatherless and the poor goes into God's law.
precepts.point: If I laughed on them, they believed it not: Job had an austere spirit. I chose out their way: he counseled and directed them. And sat chief, and dwelt as a king in the army, as one that comforteth the mourners. Job sat like a king in the army.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
“Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.” Job is telling you what he used to do. The fatherless are the orphans, and he delivered them and the ones who had no one to help.

That goes into God’s law: “He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.”

Job judged the way God judges. And he did not stop there: “The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.” When somebody is about to die and wants to speak to you, sometimes you are at a loss for words and do not know what to say to bring them comfort. Job knew exactly what to say. Then he comforted the widow, mourning and crying because her husband just died.

That is a hard thing. You have to pray to the Lord: give me the words. You have to let a dying believer know, it is going to be okay; even when you leave this world, you are going to be all right. When we die, that is not the end of it for us, and that is what comforts us.

precepts.text: Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, meaning your mind, and be no more stiffnecked, meaning hard headed. For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward.
precepts.point: In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands: when we accept Christ as our king and savior, we must circumcise all the immoralities in our hearts, in our minds. To circumcise means to cut off and get rid of. Let Christ's words circumcise our minds.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands.” The circumcision made without hands is explained in the law: “Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.” The foreskin of your heart means your mind, and stiffnecked means hard-headed.

To circumcise means to cut off and get rid of. So Moses was already calling Israel to cut away what is in the mind, not only the flesh. “For the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward.” He is the God who requires it, and he regards no man's person.

So when we accept Christ as our king and our savior, we must circumcise all the immoralities in our hearts, in our minds. Get rid of it. That is “putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ”: let Christ circumcise your mind. His words must circumcise our minds.

precepts.text: Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.
precepts.point: Romans 2 does not do away with circumcision of the flesh. Circumcision verily profiteth if thou keep the law: the Jews who grew up circumcised and keeping the law, yet broke it, made their circumcision uncircumcision; and the uncircumcised of the cast-off northern kingdom who keep the righteousness of the law are counted as circumcised. Circumcision of the heart is putting away the evil of the doings, as the prophets say, take away the foreskins of your heart; the scribes and Pharisees were clean on the outside of the cup but full of iniquity within.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.” Moses himself, who nearly died for not circumcising his son, speaks of the circumcision of the heart to a people already circumcised in the flesh.

The foreskin of the heart is stiffneckedness, the evil of the doings. Circumcision of the heart is putting that away, as the prophets say, and it stands together with the covenant of the flesh, not in place of it.

precepts.text: And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee? The first thing named is to fear the Lord thy God; that fear proves the love, the confession, and the spirit.
precepts.point: Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“And now, Israel, what doth the Lord thy God require of thee, but to fear the Lord thy God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve the Lord thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul”. The first thing named is to fear the Lord thy God.

Fear is the first spirit required, before love, before confession: that fear proves the love, the confession and the spirit. Fear and respect go hand in hand, and if you fear him you will do what he says, and do it with joyfulness and gladness for the reward no nation can touch.

That is why the Most High gathered the people at Horeb, “that they may learn to fear me all the days that they shall live upon the earth, and that they may teach their children.” Why learn to fear him? Verses 3 and 4 of this same chapter answer it: those that followed the idols were destroyed, and those that cleaved to him are alive. Follow after idols, after the nations and their religions, and he will destroy you.

precepts.text: The law of truth was in his mouth, and the priest's lips should keep knowledge, but ye are departed out of the way, ye have caused many to stumble at the law, ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi; therefore have I made you contemptible and base before all the people.
precepts.point: But they corrupted the covenant of Levi, left off teaching the law, and were partial in it, so the Lord gave them a swift and mighty judgment. Now you understand why Levi, identified in the land of Haiti, has been the poorest in the western hemisphere and catches hell to this day: their provider was the Lord, and they departed out of the way.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
At that time the Lord separated the tribe of Levi “to bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the Lord to minister unto him, and to bless in his name”, and “Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren; the Lord is his inheritance”. Malachi shows what that covenant looked like when it was kept: “The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity. For the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.”

Levi ate well through the sacrifices the Lord set up. The Levites dwelt in the best areas, the suburbs, and lived in castles, because the Lord was their provider. All they had to do was teach Israel the commandments of God: keep knowledge on their lips, and let Israel seek the law at their mouth.

“But ye are departed out of the way; ye have caused many to stumble at the law; ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith the Lord of hosts. Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people, according as ye have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law.” They left off teaching the law and were partial in it, so the Lord gave them a swift and mighty judgment: contemptible and base before all the people.

Now you understand why Levi, identified in the land of Haiti, has been the poorest in the western hemisphere and catches hell to this day. Their provider was the Lord, and they departed out of the way.

precepts.text: Talk no more so exceeding proudly, let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed; saying God knows my heart while breaking his laws is speaking proudly.
precepts.point: Do not just say you love God, put action behind it. Sisters, come out of the pants and mini skirts and put on a modest dress, and be in subjection to your own husbands; brothers, put on your fringes, stop dyeing your hair, and marry the mother of your children instead of leaving her a baby mama. When you will not do what he told you to do, no words out of your mouth can make you love him; your actions show you actually hate him.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” What the Lord requires of Israel is not talk. It is to fear him, walk in all his ways, love him, serve him with all thy heart and with all thy soul, and “keep the commandments of the Lord, and his statutes, which I command thee this day for thy good”. He is a God of knowledge, and he weighs actions, not words.

Saying God knows my heart while breaking his laws is speaking proudly; that is arrogancy coming out of the mouth. Do not just say you love God, put action behind it. Sisters, come out of the pants and mini skirts and put on a modest dress, and be in subjection to your own husbands. Brothers, put on your fringes, stop dyeing your hair, and marry the mother of your children instead of leaving her a baby mama.

When you will not do what he told you to do, no words out of your mouth can make you love him. Your actions show you actually hate him, and by him actions are weighed.

precepts.text: And this is love, that we walk after his commandments; it never changed from old covenant to new.
precepts.point: Do not just say you love God, put action behind it. Sisters, come out of the pants and mini skirts and put on a modest dress, and be in subjection to your own husbands; brothers, put on your fringes, stop dyeing your hair, and marry the mother of your children instead of leaving her a baby mama. When you will not do what he told you to do, no words out of your mouth can make you love him; your actions show you actually hate him.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
“And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.” Moses asks what the Lord requires, and it all boils down to keeping the commandments of the Lord and his statutes. John says the same: love is walking after his commandments. It never changed from old covenant to new; it is “as ye have heard from the beginning”.

Here is your purpose in life, the stipulations for the body the Most High gave you, and what you must do to please him as the children of Israel: love him and serve him with all thy heart and with all thy soul by keeping his commandments, which he commands thee for thy good. That is how you love and serve God until the day we return to the dust or he sends his son to redeem us from the land of our captivity. Loving God is not something you say; it is a walk.

precepts.text: But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend; I have taken thee from the ends of the earth, and called thee from the chief men thereof, and said, Thou art my servant; I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away.
precepts.point: No other nation can lay claim to this: our forefather Abraham was the friend of God, and the Most High took Israel from the chief men of the earth, for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were the best men walking the face of the earth when he made us a nation. Heavy scriptures right there.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
“But thou, Israel, art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.” The heaven and the heaven of heavens are the Lord's, the earth also, with all that therein is; and out of all of it, “Only the Lord had a delight in thy fathers to love them, and he chose their seed after them, even you above all people”. Our forefather Abraham was the friend of God, and Israel is the seed of that friend, chosen because the Lord delighted in the fathers.

“Thou whom I have taken from the ends of the earth, and called thee from the chief men thereof, and said unto thee, Thou art my servant; I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away.” The Most High took Israel from the chief men of the earth: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were the best men walking the face of the earth when he made us a nation. No other nation can lay claim to this. And he has not cast us away; the choosing stands “as it is this day.” Heavy scriptures right there.

precepts.text: Be not afraid of them that kill the body; but I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.
precepts.point: Christ described his father the same way and forewarned us plainly: the Most High can destroy both the flesh and the spirit, disintegrate the spirit with no second chance at life, so make sure you are walking correct and keeping these laws before you come before him.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
Moses says who Israel is dealing with: “the Lord your God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a great God, a mighty, and a terrible, which regardeth not persons, nor taketh reward”. That is what needs to be taught in the church, who we are really dealing with. Christ described his father the same way and forewarned us plainly: “Be not afraid of them that kill the body, and after that have no more that they can do. But I will forewarn you whom ye shall fear: Fear him, which after he hath killed hath power to cast into hell; yea, I say unto you, Fear him.”

Men can only kill the body. The Most High can destroy both the flesh and the spirit, disintegrate the spirit with no second chance at life. That is why the command comes first to “Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked”: make sure you are walking correct and keeping these laws before you come before him. Yea, fear him.

precepts.text: Thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; the brother becoming a stranger is the key to who Moses means.
precepts.point: The stranger of this commandment is thy brother fallen into decay, whom thou shalt relieve, not the nations Israel was commanded to drive out.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
Which stranger is Moses telling Israel to love? Obadiah gives the key: “But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction”. The brother became a stranger. Moses is prophesying of the day Israel's own brother would become a stranger: when the northern kingdom was cut off, the brother became the stranger who would come back.

“Love ye therefore the stranger: for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.” The stranger the Lord loves, “in giving him food and raiment”, is that brother who became a stranger. Love them, because they are coming back into the covenant. The commandment is not about the nations Israel was commanded to drive out; it is about thy brother.

precepts.text: If thy brother be waxen poor, then thou shalt relieve him, yea, though he be a stranger or a sojourner, that he may live with thee.
precepts.point: The stranger of this commandment is thy brother fallen into decay, whom thou shalt relieve, not the nations Israel was commanded to drive out.

note.label: Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

precepts.why:
“And if thy brother be waxen poor, and fallen in decay with thee; then thou shalt relieve him: yea, though he be a stranger, or a sojourner; that he may live with thee.” Here the law says it plainly: the stranger and the sojourner to be relieved is thy brother, waxen poor and fallen in decay. That is the stranger of this commandment, whom the Lord loves in giving him food and raiment, and whom Israel is told to love.

It is not the nations Israel was commanded to drive out. It is thy brother fallen into decay, the brother who became a stranger when the northern kingdom was cut off, and who is coming back into the covenant. Thou shalt relieve him, that he may live with thee; and remember, “ye were strangers in the land of Egypt.”

precepts.text: Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren; the Lord is his inheritance.
precepts.point: The Levites have no part among you, for the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance. The Levites were well taken care of; they dwelt in the suburbs of the cities and had the best of everything.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

precepts.why:
“Wherefore Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren; the Lord is his inheritance, according as the Lord thy God promised him.” This is why Joshua says the Levites have no part among you: the Lord himself is Levi's inheritance, and the priesthood of the Lord is his portion, according as it was promised.

Gad, Reuben and the half tribe of Manasseh had already received theirs beyond Jordan on the east from Moses, and Levi's was the Lord; so the seven parts were for the seven tribes that remained.

precepts.text: The Lord instructed Moses to hew two tables of stone like unto the first, make an ark of wood, and put in it the tables the Lord would write on.
precepts.point: So what is the ark of the covenant, and what does it contain? The Lord told Moses to hew two tables of stone like the first ones he broke, and the Lord rewrote the ten commandments on them with his own finger, and Moses put the tables in the ark. The ark of the covenant contained the commandments that God wrote.

note.label: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken

precepts.why:
The elders of Israel asked the right question: “Wherefore hath the Lord smitten us to day before the Philistines?” But instead of examining the nation, they had an idea: “Let us fetch the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of Shiloh unto us, that, when it cometh among us, it may save us out of the hand of our enemies.”

So what is the ark of the covenant, and what does it contain? “Hew thee two tables of stone like unto the first, and come up unto me into the mount, and make thee an ark of wood. And I will write on the tables the words that were in the first tables which thou brakest, and thou shalt put them in the ark.” The ark was made to hold the tables the Lord would write on.

precepts.text: Moses made an ark of shittim wood, the Lord wrote on the tables the ten commandments he spake out of the midst of the fire, and Moses put the tables in the ark, and there they be.
precepts.point: So what is the ark of the covenant, and what does it contain? The Lord told Moses to hew two tables of stone like the first ones he broke, and the Lord rewrote the ten commandments on them with his own finger, and Moses put the tables in the ark. The ark of the covenant contained the commandments that God wrote.

note.label: 1 Samuel 4: The Ark of God Is Taken

precepts.why:
“And I made an ark of shittim wood, and hewed two tables of stone like unto the first.” “And he wrote on the tables, according to the first writing, the ten commandments, which the Lord spake unto you in the mount out of the midst of the fire.” Then Moses “put the tables in the ark which I had made; and there they be, as the Lord commanded me.” The ark of the covenant contained the commandments that God wrote.

The law is spiritual, and the law has literal spiritual power; the commandments have always been our source of power as a nation. The church teaches that the laws are done away with, but watch in these chapters how seriously the Lord regarded the ark that contained his commandments.

When “the ark of the covenant of the Lord came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth rang again.” The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with it. That is how excited and ecstatic Israel was to have the ark among them; they felt their enemies could not destroy them now.

But watch why the ark did not have the effect Israel expected in this battle: there were still Israelites in the midst of idolatry with idols among them, and until those idols were put away we could not be delivered from our enemies. That is the lesson Samuel drives home in chapter 7.
